headline: Keep {control.name}. Both candidates cost {cost.uplift_range|pct} more per reply and stay in character less often.
lede: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} is clearly worse on the asked pass rate: down {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points (95% interval {reading.qwen3.8-flash.interval|pts}), inside the {aspect.margin}-point margin but not a tie. {arm:1017}'s drop of {reading.1017.change|abs|pts} points could be noise. Neither candidate improves anything this campaign measured.

flag.title: The criteria came after the results, and the judge is uncalibrated.
flag.text: The aspect, control, margin and floor were all set on {late_criteria.set_at}, after the readings were visible, and the judge has no human calibration yet (0 of 20 ratings). The cost finding is measured spend, not judged, so it supports keeping {control.name} on its own.

slots.text: **Keep {control.name}** ({control.served_model}). It has the highest pass rate ({pass_rate.September|pct}), the highest in-character rate ({judged.persona.holds_character.September|pct}) and the lowest cost ({cost_per_1k.September|usd} per 1,000 replies).

**{arm:qwen3.8-flash}:** {cost.uplift.qwen3.8-flash|pct} more per reply, in-character {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character|pts} points, pass rate {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|pts}.
**{arm:1017}:** {cost.uplift.1017|pct} more per reply, in-character {contrast.1017.persona.holds_character|pts} points.

{arm:1017} spent {reasoning_ratio.1017|pct} of its output reasoning against {control.name}'s {reasoning_ratio.September|pct}, so part of its result may be the effort budget, not the model. Latency was not compared: every run shared the machine.

Fix off-lane handling first: it is {control.name}'s weakest stratum and where both candidates lose most. Then calibrate the judge with 20 human ratings, and find out why {arm:qwen3.8-flash} cost more than the earlier campaign found.
